summary: Pilot Peak Lookout on the Stanislaus NF: CL-100 cabin on a 20-ft steel tower built 1962-63, staffed in 2012; the NHLR number and two-story kind in the brief belong to a different Pilot Peak.

facts.design: CL-100 cabin (1959 National Plan revision) atop a 20-foot K-Brace open steel tower
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Stanislaus National Forest (Groveland Ranger District)

events.note: Sonora contractor Henry Grayson was building a steel lookout tower on the peak, per a Mariposa Gazette item of 4 October 1919; the sources do not say whether it is the tower standing today
Register says the peak has been a fire detection point since at least 1921; John Hastie reported as lookout, with 63 visitors between June 6 and August 31, 1921
Barn fire in the Deer Flat district near Groveland, spotted by lookout M. Brown; a CCC fire crew confined it to three acres of grassland (item dated 6 July 1937)
Current CL-100 cabin on a 20-foot K-Brace open steel tower; the NHLR Built field reads 1962-63
Groveland district work noted in 2012 report: electrical upgrade to solar panels and batteries under way; 1,200-gallon tank water system with shower installed; fuels reduced around the site
Staffed seven days a week with a Forest Service employee, with regular maintenance (2012 report)
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: December 1, 2019

corrections.why: The Stanislaus NHLR entry describes a CL-100 cabin on a 20-foot open steel tower. The two-story hexagonal cab is the Plumas NF Pilot Peak (NHLR 600), a different lookout, so the kind appears to have come from that record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's source list includes the Plumas NF Pilot Peak page (NHLR 600, built 1976). The Stanislaus entry is NHLR 1394, the register's own entry for this site, and is the one used.

The Register dates the present cabin to 1962-63. A 1919 Gazette item shows a steel lookout tower under construction on the peak. The sources do not say whether the two are the same structure, so the 1919 item is recorded as a separate event.

notes_for_editor: Newest staffing and condition evidence is the 2012 chapter report; current staffing, condition and public access are unconfirmed. The brief's access 'unknown' is omitted rather than filled in, because no access route was readable: the trailforks Pilot Peak Road listing returned HTTP 403. The brief's 2012 'modified' event is supported, but the report calls the work in progress, so the story says so. The 2012 report also has a separate 'Pilot - Not staffed' entry in another district's list; the text read does not tie it to this lookout, so it is not used. The 1962 build is recorded as 1962, the start of the NHLR's 1962-63 range. The height of 20 feet is converted to 6.1 m. No photos were added: the NHLR page's 2010 photo credit is to Ron Kemnow and the license is not stated.
